sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Apple announced plans to alter macOS privacy settings, requiring very explicit user action before apps gain full-disk access. This follows claims by columnist Jason Aten that Meta's AI agent, Muse, read his Apple Messages without permission. Meta disputed this, stating message access is opt-in and requires enabling both full-disk access and a Messages connector setting. However, macOS security expert Patrick Wardle noted that full-disk access allows any non-root file to be read.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Full-disk access was created to let backup apps work properly by sidestepping standard privacy controls. Apple warned that developers are using it in ways that expose files, mail, messages, and browsing history. The company stated that as AI agents become more autonomous, the risks associated with this level of system access will grow substantially.
